items.discussion: tools-52 (Order 52); M141's measurement, callgrind on kolt's client `check src/client.vl`, profiling build of 697c9517 + M141's commit, the const table warm; sweeps/order52/tools-52/ (callgrind outputs not kept)
items.title: M141's residue: the warm const pass on kolt's client is still ~187 M instructions after the S half (was 210 M) - the whole-program capability check refines dispatch a SECOND time (36 M beside the context pass's 71 M), the Expr::Local scan is 20 M, the per-site reach closure 17.5 M, the world's drop 5.8 M - and M141's premise (a rebuilt ConstWorld, a re-walked reach) was wrong
items.body: Measured with callgrind (inclusive instructions, `const_eval::evaluate` = 210 M of a 8,832 M cold-ish client check): evaluate_one 107 M (ConstWorld::prepare 42 M = walk_entity 16.5 + reach_from 17.5 + prelude; const_cache::evaluate 32 M = ChannelCall::ask 12.5 + reads/clones; free_locals 30 M), check_const_only 70 M (refined_edges 36 M, candidates_of 17.5 M, self 16 M), ConstWorld drop 5.8 M, live_tokens_of 5.7 M, ConstWorld::new 4.4 M. The item's two hypotheses were already true: ConstWorld is built ONCE per `evaluate` (4 M, the seed only), and the reach walk is computed once per site (169 reach_from calls for 166 sites, no retry on the warm path). M141's S half (shipped): `candidates_of` memoised per (import scope, name) (-13 M), the refined edges built lazily (a program with no runtime path to a channel verb pays none - kolt's has one through std's style functions), the explicit pass's local index holds only the locals inside a const expression (-10 M); 210 M -> 187 M, -0.28 % of the check. Left, ranked: (1) `dispatch_refine::refined_edges` runs twice per analysis - the context pass (71 M) and the const check (36 M) - and both pay the same program-wide scans (`call_subject_entities`, `value_taken` over the whole entity map, and `impl_members_for_bound` 39 M for the const call alone, keyed by (subject type, member, traits) and so shareable across the two calls and across sites): one per-analysis cache in dispatch_refine.rs would take most of the 36 M and a good part of the 71 M (the two calls' site lists differ - the const check's candidates are un-narrowed - so share the per-(type, member, bound) memo, not the result). (2) `free_locals` still scans the whole entity map once (20 M): the analyzer already walks every const expression, so recording a const expression's `Expr::Local` references there (analyzer core) removes the scan. (3) `ConstWorld::reach_from` (17.5 M): sites share a large sub-closure (the style chain), so a memo per EmissionId (or an SCC close) beats re-walking `requires` per site. (4) The ConstWorld's drop (5.8 M) and `live_tokens_of` (5.7 M, the item's own memo suggestion) are small. Expected after (1)-(3): the warm pass under ~20 ms (it is ~26 ms now: 29 ms before the S half at load 2.5). Owner: dispatch_refine.rs/context.rs are the solver lane's, the recording is the analyzer core's.

items.title: seal.sh's default `VILAN_PERF_KOLT_COMMIT=984a1dfb` (the v0.44.0 seal's base) pre-dates the mirrored-store exhibit: on the default, N174's harness now SKIPS `parse break` (and `model.vl keystroke`'s References probe lands on nothing) on the BASE side and the seal is RED on a skipped mandate row
items.body: By design: the base side's `--commit` archive of 984a1dfb lacks `channel_name.adopt(channel.current_name());`, so `parse break` / `parse repair` skip there and `perf_gate.py seal` is red on the base-side skip of a mandate row (nothing to compare the tip against). The seal's mechanics already say the base kolt is a clone COPY of the owner's tree (dee494ab or later) committed inside the copy - so the seal runs with `VILAN_PERF_KOLT_DIR` and `VILAN_PERF_KOLT_COMMIT` set and never meets the default - but the default is a trap for the next person to run `seal.sh` bare. Fix: drop the default (refuse with the message, like `VILAN_PERF_KOLT_DIR=... is not a directory`), or move it to the exhibit's commit. Also `shared.vl keystroke` is still anchored on text 984a1dfb and today's tree both hold, so it is unaffected.

items.title: B619's instance now exists as a repro: a derive whose GENERATED impl imports `std::path::basename` mints `std::path` in the drain's second round (`VILAN_COUNTERS=1` reads `late-round-mints=1`), and writing the same import beside it mints it in the first - the two spellings emit DIFFERENT bundles (`now` and `basename` swap places), verified under 0.49.0
items.body: The counter (B619, `counters::late_round_mints`) is zero on kolt's two legs, the eleven examples and every corpus file, and 1 on the repro (sweeps/order52/tools-52/finds/b619_generated_only_module.vl: a `[derive(Leafy)]` whose generated impl writes `import std::path::basename;`, beside a written `import std::time::now;`). `vilan build` of that program and of the same program with a redundant written `import std::path::basename;` differ: with the generated-only module minted in round two `now` is emitted before `basename`, with the written import after - B603 fixed the written-import case, this is the generated-only case it left, and the estate has no instance. The clean fix is the one B619 names - defer SourceId attribution of the registry's and the expansion's diagnostics until the last round and mint the generated-only modules in the first canonical order - or, cheaper, resolve a macro's generated `std::`/`pkg::` references before the first round's minting (the macro epilogue runs after it, so this is a re-order of the drain). Until then the std-prefix P3 key check (closure over WRITTEN imports) refuses a world with late-round mints. No action needed while the estate reads zero.
